_doc.purpose: Component + behaviour spec for the Inspector panel / coding-verifier layer — the generalised successor to viewer_internals.json (which documented the old margin-shift evidence viewer). This file describes WHAT the layer does and the contracts it depends on; you build the panel per inspector_panel_reference.html, you do not reimplement it from scratch. The whole layer is MANDATORY for every blog.
_doc.predecessor: Generalises an earlier margin-shift evidence viewer (retired — not shipped). The old layer shifted body content with body.margin-right; the Inspector panel uses a no-reflow overlay drawer instead (see drawer.no_reflow).
_doc.data_source: The panel reads two inline <script> islands embedded in index.html: verifyMap (per-element provenance) and runCells (in-browser snippets). Those islands MUST be byte-identical to verify/verify_map.json and verify/run_cells.json (see inline_byte_identical).
_doc.mandatory: Every published blog ships this layer. A blog without a working Inspector panel + a clean reproducible notebook is incomplete.

kinds_to_renderers._note: verify_map[id].kind selects the drawer renderer. Kinds: computation / media / generated / fact, plus 'credits' (a fact-shaped license/source aggregator rendered with a Credits badge) — matching verify_map.schema.json.
kinds_to_renderers.computation: Renders the claim, the code slice (code_file + code_lines), a data_preview table, the expected_output, and a Run panel. If run_cells[id].runnable, a 'Run' button executes the snippet in-browser (lazy Pyodide) and grades it; otherwise the code is shown read-only with a pointer to the notebook (full_ref).
kinds_to_renderers.media: Renders the asset preview (image/video/audio_embed/audio) plus source_url, license, author and identity. For a multi-asset element, renders the gallery (see gallery).
kinds_to_renderers.generated: Renders the AI-generated preview plus tool, model, full prompt, purpose and disclosure, and surfaces real_default as the publish-safe fallback (the real asset is the default; the AI asset is opt-in / a toggle).
kinds_to_renderers.fact: Renders the claim, its category, and the categorised sources[] — each source as a titled link with its facts[] bullet list.
kinds_to_renderers.credits: A fact-shaped license/source aggregator (e.g. a card-deck's data + photo licences) rendered with a 'Credits' badge; uses the same renderer as fact.

drawer.no_reflow: The drawer OVERLAYS the page (fixed-position panel above the content); it does NOT push the body. This replaces the old viewer's `body { margin-right: 440px }` reflow, which caused full-bleed (100vw) sections to mis-size and the page to jump on open. The body stays exactly where it is.
drawer.open_on_element: Clicking any element carrying a data-* id from verify_map opens the drawer for that id and renders the matching kind.
drawer.focus_trap: While open, focus is trapped inside the drawer (Tab cycles within it); focus returns to the triggering element on close.
drawer.escape_and_dismiss: Esc closes the drawer; clicking the scrim / a close control also closes it. Closing restores focus.
drawer.es5_safe: Panel JS stays compatible with the blog's own scripts (no global leaks; avoid clobbering the page's identifiers), consistent with the self-contained file:// constraint inherited from the old viewer.

runnable_snippets.lazy_pyodide: Pyodide is loaded LAZILY — only on the first 'Run' click — so the page's initial load is not penalised. Subsequent runs reuse the loaded runtime.
runnable_snippets.imports: Snippets import only numpy / pandas / stdlib (the Pyodide-safe set declared in run_cells.schema.json).

grading.pass: Exact / derived snippets (reduced_n == null): stdout must equal expected_stdout -> PASS.
grading.approximate: Stochastic snippets (reduced_n set): the reduced-N run is graded '≈ within noise' against the published figure and is NEVER shown as a hard PASS. The exact full-N reproduction is the notebook cell named in full_ref.
grading.read_only: needs_network:true => runnable:false: the snippet is shown read-only with a note pointing to the notebook; the panel does not execute it.

gallery.keys_in_order: A multi-asset element exposes its gallery under one of three keys tried IN THIS ORDER: flags || assets || photos. The first present non-empty array is rendered.
gallery.item_shape: Each item follows verify_map.schema.json#/$defs/galleryItem and carries its OWN source_url + license so per-asset attribution is preserved in the gallery view.
gallery.caption: Item caption falls back across label -> team -> name -> subject -> filename.

data_attr_contract.attrs: Elements are bound to provenance via data-* attributes, one per producing role: data-ana, data-det, data-des, data-sct, data-cin. The attribute value is the atomic id (e.g. data-ana="ana_01").
data_attr_contract.decorative_skip: Purely decorative elements carry no data-* id and are skipped by the panel (no drawer, no scan warning).
data_attr_contract.innermost_wins: When data-* attributes nest, the INNERMOST element that was clicked wins — its id selects the drawer, not an ancestor's.
data_attr_contract.ids_must_exist: Every data-* id present in the page MUST exist as a key in verify_map.json. A data-* id with no verify_map entry is an auditor failure (dangling reference); a verify_map id with no element on the page is an unused entry (report, not fatal).

inline_byte_identical.rule: The verifyMap and runCells <script> islands inlined into index.html MUST be byte-identical to verify/verify_map.json and verify/run_cells.json respectively.
inline_byte_identical.why: The on-disk JSON files are the auditable source of truth and the publish artifacts (also the inputs the downloaded notebook reproduces from); the inline copies are what the panel actually reads at runtime. If they drift, the audited provenance no longer matches what readers see.
inline_byte_identical.escaping: When inlining, escape any literal </script> as <\/script> to avoid premature script-tag closure, and serialise with ensure_ascii so raw multibyte chars / newlines do not break the JS parser (inherited from the old viewer's constraints).

publish_wiring.NB_PATH: Path/URL to the reproducible notebook (verify/<topic>_forecast.ipynb) that the panel's 'Download notebook' link points at. The reader downloads it and runs it LOCALLY (alongside the bundled verify/data/ inputs) to reproduce the numbers from raw data. There is NO Colab branch — the notebook is download-and-run-locally only.
publish_wiring.open_cell_source: The panel's 'Open the notebook cell ↗' button (openCellSource) opens a fresh blank tab containing a tiny self-contained HTML page that renders the inlined run_cells[id].code in a styled <pre> — a RAW-CODE page, NOT a Colab/notebook link. It works on file:// with no assets and shows exactly the cell behind the clicked claim. (The in-browser Pyodide 'Run in your browser' path and the 'Download notebook' link are the other two ways to run the code.)
publish_wiring.viewer_redirect: The Inspector panel lives IN index.html (the in-page layer; the panel + the verifyMap/runCells islands are embedded there) — that single file IS the verifiable artifact. New runs ship ONLY index.html; no separate viewer.html is emitted. (Historically the Inspector emitted a viewer.html redirect for paper-link continuity; that was retired. Previously-deployed blogs keep their own standalone viewer.html on disk, unaffected.)
publish_wiring.bundle: The publish step must also bundle the notebook's inputs under verify/data/ (next to the notebook, so the DATA_DIR resolver finds them on disk) and any code/*.json the notebook reads (see reproducible_notebook.md §6).
